newsitem.title: USA: JumboSports falls after lackluster Q1.
newsitem.headline: JumboSports falls after lackluster Q1.

text.p: Shares of JumboSports Inc fell Thursday after the sports company posted weaker-than-expected first quarter earnings.

The stock fell about eight percent, losing 3/8 to 4-3/8 after it posted a first quarter loss of $0.07 a share compared with a loss of $0.02 last year. Same store sales for the period fell about 11.6 percent for the Tampa, Fla.-based company, which operates 85 sporting goods superstores in 29 states.

"The first quarter was a disappointment for JumboSports and one in which we had expected some incremental improvement. Clearly, this was a surprise to us," said company chairman Stephen Bebis. He cited softness in the industry, particularly in fitness and footwear.

Raymond James & Associates analyst Harry Katica, who had expected a smaller quarterly loss of $0.02 a share, cut his rating of the stock from buy to neutral and reduced estimates for 1997 and 1998 after the earnings release.
"The company has made positive strides ... but recent results continue to be lackluster and sales trends have yet to display any material improvement," he said.

Katica cited sluggish growth in the overall sporting goods industry for the downgrade but also noted the company's large debt load. Long-term debt was $290 million at the end of the first quarter while shareholders' equity was $159 million.
He also said JumboSports delayed the roll-out of some new marketing and merchandising initiatives, which pushed out the timing of the company's expected earnings recovery.
The company was called Sports & Recreation until it changed its name to JumboSports on February 14. It was formerly traded under the symbol "WON".
